lines.text: Genesis 8: 22
While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat,
summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease.
I
AFter many cold and depressing weeks, the sun of spring
has begun to cheer us with its radiance and warmth. The
vital forces of nature, long frozen and paralysed, have at last
burst forth freely; trees and bushes have adorned themselves
with the splendour of their blossom, and the trees are once
more green. As the farmer in the surrounding country has
been glad to be able to get down to his work in earnest, we
town-dwellers too have felt an impulse of grateful joy. Our
work, of course, unlike that of the farmer, is not dependent
on the weather; nevertheless, we rejoice once more in the
coming of the spring. We rejoice not merely because the
prosperity of all of us depends on the undisturbed continu-
ance of the processes of nature so that the earth may bring
forth its fruit. Our own pleasure in the spring is much more
immediate and instinctive, and needs no special justification.
And, too, the more our lives are harnessed to work, responsi-
bility and care, the more we feel it as a release to be able to
open ourselves freely to the light and beauty of the spring,
when there takes place a veritable renaissance in the world
of nature which speaks to us with an audible voice.
No doubt there are people who do not hear this voice and
do not feel things in this way. But feeling certain that our
joy in the spring is right and healthy we know that there is
something lacking to these people, that there is something
morose and crabbed about them and that this lack infects
